findings: F-01 HARD (P3; HF-06 class, independently reproduced at the pinned hash): the exact quantifier prefix and the conclusion block expand DIFFERENT visibility predicates. quantifiers.formal (schemas/af_wcc_vacuum.yaml:54-55) closes with 'not exists q in I+ with gamma subset J^-(q) intersect M' and quantifiers.domains.D5 (:79-81) defines q by 'gamma([0,T)) is contained in the causal past J^-(q)' - both are WHOLE-CURVE single-q containment. The class's one canonical predicate, visibility.definition (:219-220), is the single-q TAIL predicate ('exists q in I+ AND t0 in [0,T) such that the TAIL gamma([t0,T)) is contained in J^-(q)'), and conclusion.statement_formal (:251) binds that predicate by name. hard_failures.finding: Operative quantifier expansion contradicts the canonical visibility predicate (whole curve vs tail). quantifiers.formal (lines 47-55, decisive clause at 54-55: 'not exists q in I+ with gamma subset J^-(q) intersect M') and domain D5 (lines 79-81: q such that 'gamma([0,T)) is contained in ... J^-(q)') use whole-curve single-q non-containment, and quantifiers.ordered (56-62) binds no t0. visibility.definition (line 220) defines visibility with the tail ('exists q in I+ AND t0 in [0,T) such that the TAIL gamma([t0,T)) is contained in J^-(q)') and visibility.negation_conclusion (line 222) is the matching tail negation ('for every q in I+ and every t0 in [0,T), the tail ... is NOT contained'). Since whole-curve containment A(q) implies tail containment B(q,t0) and not conversely, 'not exists q A(q)' is STRICTLY WEAKER than 'not exists q exists t0 B(q,t0)'. quantifiers.negation (84-88) negates the tail predicate ('some ... geodesic ... is visible from I+'), so the formal block and its declared negation are not complements of each other. The R1-F02 tail correction was propagated to the visibility block (R1 tags at 220/222, note at 227) but not into quantifiers.formal/ordered/D5; the earlier whole-curve reading survives in the operative statement and in statement_formal (line 251) only as the undefined symbol AF_{I+}.
